Premise-first for the dispatching seat/dev: verify the installed `@objectstack/spec` (17.0.0 GA pin) actually carries `ObjectNavItemSchema.runAction` before coding — merged 08-10 predates the GA publish, so it is expected present, but verify rather than inherit; if absent, report `premise_still_valid: false` and re-block on the next pin bump. Also per the retired framework card's work list: the framework liveness ledger row flip (`planned`/`authorWarn` → `live` with a NavigationRenderer evidence pointer) lands framework-side — when this card's PR is accepted, the accepting seat files that follow-up in objectstack with a `Blocked-by:` back-link, per the cross-repo follow-up rule.

Nothing widens. ⚠️ If your measurement says the declared slot cannot carry what the private convention carried, that is a fork — **stop and report**, do not extend the spec from here.
Serial constraints cleared: `packages/layout` + `packages/i18n` were freed this round (PR5346 merged); `packages/app-shell`'s layout subtree was touched by PR5339 and PR5346 — **rebase on current `main` and re-read before you plan.**

## ⛔ ZONE 0 — a hard premise gate. Do this before writing a single line.

The unlock scan says the blocker `objectstack-ai/objectstack#7253` is a **merged** spec PR (2026-08-10, **pre-GA**), so the declared `runAction` slot is *expected* to be in the `17.0.0` pin. **Expected is not measured.** Verify against the **installed** package:

```
node --input-type=module -e "import {ObjectNavItemSchema} from '@objectstack/spec/ui';
  console.log(Object.keys(ObjectNavItemSchema.shape ?? {}).includes('runAction'))"
```

(adjust the import path/symbol to whatever the nav item schema is actually exported as — finding it is part of the check).

- **Present ⇒ proceed.**
- **Absent ⇒ STOP.** Report `premise_still_valid: false` and say so plainly; ⛔ do not work around it by declaring the key objectui-side.

⚠️ **Counter-probe the answer either way** — probe a key you know that schema has, through the same call. A probe that returns `false` because the import path was wrong looks identical to a probe that returns `false` because the key is missing. That exact trap voided two readings on #5042 this week (once `node_modules` was absent so probe *and* control were empty; once the filename was `view.ts` instead of `view.zod.ts`).

**Why I am this insistent**: two cards this round were stopped by precisely this gap — **merged upstream ≠ published ≠ pinned here**, three distinct states. `GanttConfigSchema.viewMode` (#5074) and `ListMapConfigSchema` (#5042) are both merged on objectstack `main` and both **invisible** to this repo, because they landed *after* the `17.0.0` GA cut and the changeset backlog is unreleased. Both now sit behind **#5328**. Your card's blocker merged **before** the cut, which is why it is expected to be fine — but that is an argument, not a reading. If it turns out absent, this card joins #5328 and I will re-block it.

## The work, once the gate passes

Consume the **declared** `runAction` slot and retire the private `?runAction=<name>` string convention. The point is the same one this repo keeps relearning: a private convention that no schema declares is a second de-facto contract, invisible to every gate — and here the spec has already published the real one, so the convention is pure debt.

- Report **what the private convention could express that the declared slot cannot**, if anything. That is the fork condition; if the answer is "nothing", say so with the evidence.
- ⛔ Do not leave a compatibility shim that keeps reading `?runAction=` "just in case" unless you can name a producer that still emits it — and if you can, that producer is the real work, not the shim.

## Cross-repo follow-up — file it, don't just mention it

Per the unlock scan and the cross-repo rule: when this lands, the framework's **liveness ledger row** flips (`planned`/`authorWarn` → `live`, with a `NavigationRenderer` evidence pointer) **on the objectstack side**. That follow-up is filed in `objectstack-ai/objectstack` with a `Blocked-by:` back-link to this card. **I will file it when I accept the PR** — you do not need to, but say in your report whether your implementation actually gives that row its evidence pointer, and where.

## Tests

- A nav item declaring `runAction` runs that action on navigation.
- The **private `?runAction=` string no longer drives anything** — this is the retirement; it must fail before your edit.
- An undefined action name behaves as the spec says (the upstream schema already rejects a `runAction` naming an undefined action — `defineStack` throws *"deep-link references action '…' (via runAction)"*; check what the **client** should do and pin it).
- Nothing else in the nav path regresses — `packages/layout`'s `NavigationRenderer` just had its dead label resolvers removed (PR5346); read that change before touching the file.

Reverse-verify: restore the consumer, keep the tests, **predict which go red before running**, report predicted vs observed. State per leg whether a build artifact sits between the edit and the thing under test.

## Gates

Derive from your diff (`scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is **objectstack-only**). Run vitest **from the repo root** — the reason is not that package-scoped runs are refused (17 packages own a standalone `vitest.config.ts` and are not refused) but that a package-scoped run uses **a different config than CI does**. If you add user-visible copy, expect `check:i18n-keys` / `check:i18n-drift` and all ten locale packs. Changeset per `check-changeset-presence.mjs`'s verdict; `patch` or `minor`, ⛔ **never `major`**.

⛔ Do not background a long check and end your turn. ⛔ No exhaustive paginated API sweeps.

## Deliver

Draft PR against `main`, first body line `Fixes #5216`. **Put the Zone 0 probe's output in the PR body** — it is the reason the card was dispatchable. Push the branch early. Return the JSON report and post it as a comment whose first line is the literal `<!-- os-dev-report -->` marker.

**Liveness-ledger evidence pointer (asked for explicitly):** yes, the implementation gives that row real evidence, and it is split across two files rather than the single `NavigationRenderer` pointer the card anticipated:

- **producer** — `packages/layout/src/NavigationRenderer.tsx`: `NAV_RUN_ACTION_PARAM` (the param name's one definition) and `withRunAction`, applied inside `resolveHref`'s `object` branch on the list landings only.
- **consumer** — `packages/app-shell/src/hooks/useNavRunAction.ts`, wired generically at `packages/app-shell/src/views/ObjectView.tsx` (every object list) and, with the extra entitlement gate, at `packages/app-shell/src/environment/EnvironmentListToolbar.tsx`.

A `NavigationRenderer`-only pointer would overstate it in one direction and understate it in the other: `NavigationRenderer` writes the deep link but never runs anything, and the thing that makes the row genuinely `live` — an actual shell consuming the declared slot — lives in `app-shell`. Worth carrying both into the objectstack follow-up.
